name: slower-tempo-more-air
style: East Coast boom-bap from the back end of the nineties, a lone big-bodied rapper taking his time: laid-back, relaxed pacing, he drags each line a hair behind the snare and lets the last word hang, wide breathing room between lines, unbothered conversational tone, a deliberate beat of silence held just ahead of every punchline. Voice: a huge-framed man, deep smooth baritone from the chest, slurred Brooklyn vowels, a short asthmatic wheeze on each intake of breath, dry, close to the mic. Instrumental: 82 BPM, swung dusty breakbeat with a thick knocking kick and a hard flat snare, a melancholy after-midnight Rhodes-and-organ soul-jazz figure sliced into a cold, menacing minor loop, walking acoustic-bass-style bottom end, tape hiss and crackle; in the gap after each rule a gravelly chopped-up group shout calls out the next number; bare, minimal, threatening, no hook
exclude: double-time flow, crammed syllables, rushed delivery, sung chorus, female vocals, autotune
lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.
[pause]

[Verse 1]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.
[pause]

[Verse 2]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.
[pause]

[Verse 3]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.
[pause]

[Verse 4]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.
[pause]

[Verse 5]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.
[pause]

[Verse 6]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.
[pause]

[Verse 7]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.
[pause]

[Verse 8]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.
[pause]

[Verse 9]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.
[pause]

[Verse 10]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.
[pause]

[Outro]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
